threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You’ll spot the newbies at the local market, fumbling with cash while everyone else knows the swipe-and-run routine.
The 63 bus last night had a guy loudly convincing everyone he was the next big garage artist, while half the passengers just nodded off.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw the bakery owner hand a fresh loaf to a kid on a bike while arguing with the pizza guy over the best tomato sauce. That’s Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you can find mini-donkey rides at some street festivals. Hilarious and totally unexpected!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their casual shrug when the BART's down – while newcomers lose their minds over delays.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy chatting with his reflection in the bus window, pretending they were on a talk show. Totally unfazed by the chaos outside.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just pop into a trendy bar and find a spot anytime. Good luck getting any space at La Monda without a reservation!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their habit of apologizing for their Spanish, even when it's perfectly fine.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers—they're the ones waiting at dawn for a bus, oblivious that the 48 doesn't run on weekends.
Caught a guy on the 47 last night, singing to his takeaway like it was a lost love. The bus was packed but everyone was trying not to make eye contact.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting in a café, I watched a guy casually juggle flaming torches while a couple debated the best döner spots. Berlin feels real in these moments.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a late-night Kebab shop where the owner also hosts book readings. The scent of spice and poetry fills the air.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their ability to seamlessly navigate BART delays without breaking a sweat, while newbies just stare at the screen puzzled.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a local artist sketching the bus stop crowd—felt like a snapshot of city life amidst the usual chaos. That’s SF!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think all locals flock to Park Güell. In reality, we hide away in lesser-known plazas like Plaça de la Vila, sipping coffee and enjoying the peace.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll catch them taking a selfie at every plaça, not realizing locals avoid it like the midday sun. Classic signs of the new wave.
